the_merge:
PR #181 merged as d10820867212de8bf727d66defa4fee35ca07926. The four required contexts were earned by RE-RUNNING each gate's own pull_request run for the exact head 69466353eccc, which returned on attempt 2 with event=pull_request preserved, all four green.

THE DECISIVE OBSERVATION IS ONE WORD. On the dispatch mechanism this pull request sat at mergeable_state=blocked with four green check runs under the required names, from app 15368, on its head. On the re-run mechanism the same pull request read mergeable_state=CLEAN. The ruleset counted the re-run's checks and had never counted the dispatch's. That is the whole difference between the two designs, and it is visible in one field.

The merge is a true merge commit (parents b798b085, 69466353), performed with the sha PINNED so GitHub would refuse it if anything had moved, with 0 unresolved review threads, under an unweakened ruleset: four required contexts still pinned to integration 15368, no bypass actors, merge-commits-only, strict up-to-date policy, review-thread resolution required.
how_it_was_driven_stated_exactly:
The orchestrator WORKFLOW on master still contained the retired dispatch runner, because a pull_request workflow runs from the HEAD BRANCH while a scheduled workflow runs from the default branch. That asymmetry is precisely why Option E can bootstrap and the dispatch model could not -- and it means this proof was driven by running the BRANCH's scripts/ci/nightly-orchestrate.py against the live GitHub API, not by the 03:10 scheduled run. Same code, same decision module, same API calls, same protected merge. From tonight the scheduled workflow on master is the Option E orchestrator and drives it unattended.

Stated because the distinction is exactly the kind that gets glossed into 'the nightly run merged it'. It did not; the nightly runner did, invoked by hand.
the_refusals_were_observed_not_simulated:
Three, none of them manufactured:

  A FAILED GATE, twice. The first authoritative attempt refused with GATES_NOT_ALL_GREEN because the PR body cited T0183 rather than T0184, the receipt that now grants the phase status -- the one authoritative surface that is not committed, so no tree-only check can catch it. The second refused because the mutation suite's BASELINE failed: structural=0 keyword=1. Both times three gates were green, one was red, and nothing merged.

  A NEWER COMMIT INVALIDATING A PRIOR RESULT. After the corrected head was pushed, tools/nightly-status.py reported SUPERSEDED_FAILURE for the earlier red night and stated that nothing was owed because the head had moved -- exit 0, not a stale demand for repair.

  NO EVIDENCE REUSE ON THE AUTHORITATIVE ATTEMPT, verbatim from the runner: 'this run is the NIGHTLY AUTHORITATIVE VALIDATION (correlation attempt-3). -> NO REUSE: the nightly authoritative validation must execute every gate step freshly; earlier evidence -- including a previous night's -- may never substitute for it.'
the_daytime_cost_measured_rather_than_cl:
On two separate pushes, four pull_request runs at attempt 1, each executing ONE step and failing: 7-8s and 7-11s per gate, about 31s across all four, against the 29-31 MINUTES a push cost before. In the governance gate 33 of 35 steps were skipped; in phase3, 46 of 48. No checkout, no Go build, no PostgreSQL, no browser, no mutation matrix.

And the two properties that matter held: all four required contexts were REPORTED, so the ruleset could be evaluated, and all four were NON-PASSING, so nothing could merge on them.
a_verdict_is_about_the_tree_it_RAN_again:
The second refusal was mine and it is the transferable lesson of this receipt. ZERO_STALE_LEFTOVERS = PASS was obtained, and then T0184 and the packs were committed on top of it, and the earlier PASS was relied on for the tree that was pushed. The tree had changed underneath the result.

The concrete failure: `render` rewrote 00-START-HERE.md and PROJECT-INSTRUCTIONS.md, both of which carry generated blocks, and the build-packs run that followed kept a stale SOURCE_COMMIT instead of recording the new head -- so the pack MANIFEST carried checksums for the previous content of files that had already changed. Two mismatches, and the mutation suite refused the GOOD state before applying any mutation.

The ordering that makes it true: commit everything, THEN rebuild the packs at that head, THEN let the manifest list the result. This is the same error family as the dispatch over-claim in T0184: a signal was read as evidence about something it was not about.
the_correction_this_receipt_carries:
tools/nightly-status.py printed, as the first thing CLAUDE.md tells every session to read: 'the delivery head has moved to no open candidate since'. Not a sentence. An empty candidate list joined into a message written for a non-empty one.

The VERDICT was correct throughout -- superseded, nothing owed, exit 0 -- and the zero-candidate case was ALREADY COVERED BY A TEST. That is why it survived: the test asserted the boolean and said nothing about the text. The reason string is not decoration; it is the entire output of the session-start check, and a malformed sentence there is a malformed instruction. Two reasons now read as two sentences, and both are asserted -- 83 assertions, up from 81.

a_copied_claim_is_still_a_claim:
previous_state and new_state were copied wholesale from T0184, which carried 'This increment performed controlled acceptance ON the PRE-LIVE appliance'. Copied into a repository-only receipt that itself states PRE-LIVE was never contacted, it made this record contradict itself about operational history -- caught in review, not by a validator.

Both values now describe what this increment actually did. The mechanism is worth naming: inheriting a field because it was 'unchanged' is not the same as the CLAIM in it still being true.
